# Pulse — Full Technical Guide

## 1. Summary

Pulse is a native macOS code editor written in Swift and AppKit. Its design constraint is memory: about 60–70 MB in everyday use, and a hard limit of 100 MB enforced on every build. It uses no CPU while idle.

- Developer: Suraj Pisal
- License: MIT
- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon and Intel
- Repository: https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse
- Website: https://pulse0.app

---

## 2. Features

- **Folders and files**: open a folder (⌘O), browse it in a sidebar file tree (the active file stays highlighted and its folders open to show it), open files in tabs, with a path bar (breadcrumbs) above each file. Folders are read only when expanded. New file, new folder, reveal in Finder, copy path and move to Trash from the tree's context menu.
- **Windows**: one window per folder (⇧⌘N for a new one); opening a folder that is already open brings its window forward.
- **Split editors**: Split Editor Right (⌥⌘\) or Split Editor Down, from the View menu, the command palette or a tab's right-click menu, which also has Close and Close Others. Splits nest into a grid. A file open in two panes is one document: one copy of its text, one undo history, and edits show in both. A pane closes with its last tab.
- **Syntax highlighting**: Swift, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C/C++/Objective-C, Java/Kotlin/Scala/Dart/C#, Ruby, shell, HTML/XML, CSS/SCSS, JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown and SQL. Regex-based, not a full parser.
- **Editing**: line numbers, current-line highlight, auto-indent (including after `{`, `[`, `(` and Python `:`), spaces for tabs, toggle line comment (⌘/), indent and outdent (⌘] and ⌘[), word wrap (⌥⌘W), font size (⌘+, ⌘−, ⌘0).
- **Code folding**: by indentation, as in VS Code, so it works in every language. A chevron in the gutter (shown on hover; always on a folded line) or ⌥⌘[ / ⌥⌘] folds and unfolds the block at the caret; View › Folding and the command palette also have Fold All and Unfold All. A folded line ends in "⋯", which unfolds it on click. The closing brace stays visible, the text is unchanged, and folds are not saved between launches.
- **Find and replace**: the standard macOS find bar (⌘F, ⌥⌘F, ⌘G, ⌘E).
- **Project search** (⇧⌘F): runs ripgrep (`rg`) as a short-lived child process when installed, otherwise a built-in scan. Results grouped by file; click to jump to the match. The `…` button shows "files to include" and "files to exclude": comma-separated globs as in VS Code (`*.ts`, `src`, `./src`, `src/**/*.test.ts`, `*.{ts,tsx}`), case-insensitive; a folder pattern covers everything inside it, and an exclude beats an include.
- **Command palette**: ⌘P go to file (fuzzy), ⇧⌘P commands, ⌘L go to line.
- **Integrated terminal** (⌃`): your login shell via SwiftTerm, created on first use. New Terminal (⌃⇧`) adds a tab, Split Terminal (⌘\) a pane beside the current one; each has its own shell. Hiding the panel keeps the shells running; "Kill Terminal" ends the focused one.
- **Source control** (⌃⇧G): staged and unstaged changes for the open folder's Git repository, with buttons to stage (+) or unstage (−) a file or a whole section. A click on a changed file opens its diff in a tab; a double-click opens the file. Status and diffs come from short-lived `git` processes, run only while the panel is on screen or when asked.
- **Claude Code**: run `claude` in Pulse's terminal and it connects to the window the way it connects to VS Code, so it sees the open file and the lines you select. ⇧⌘K (View › Send Selection to Claude Code) sends the selection as an @-mention to the `claude` running in the focused terminal, and `/ide` connects a `claude` started in another terminal. The connection listens on 127.0.0.1 only, needs a per-window token, starts only if Claude Code is installed (`~/.claude` exists), and can be turned off with View › Share Selection with Claude Code. Pulse has no built-in AI features of its own.
- **`pulse` command**: `pulse .` opens the current folder, `pulse a.swift src/` opens files and folders. Release builds add the command on first launch; Pulse › Install 'pulse' Command adds it later.
- **Read-only files** (the default): files opened from disk can't be typed into until you click Read Only in the status bar or choose File › Read Only. Welcome › Default file mode switches the default to Edit. New files and restored unsaved text are always editable.
- **Autosave** (on by default): modified files with a path are written one second after typing stops, when Pulse loses focus, and at quit.
- **Session recovery**: the open folder, tabs, cursor positions and the text of unsaved buffers are stored in `~/Library/Application Support/Pulse/session.json` and restored at launch.
- **External changes**: files changed on disk are reloaded when Pulse regains focus, if they have no unsaved edits.
- **Resource meter**: the status bar shows the Git branch, Pulse's own physical footprint and CPU, and the footprint of shells it started, separately.
- **Preferences**: rebind any command in Pulse › Keyboard Shortcuts (⌥⌘K) or as JSON; separate font sizes for the editor, terminal and sidebar; light, dark or auto appearance.
- **Updates**: release builds check GitHub for a new release at launch and at most once a day; Pulse › Check for Updates… checks on demand. An update replaces the app in place and reopens it with your tabs.

Not included by design: extensions, a full Git client (history, merges), debugger, language servers, built-in AI features, telemetry, accounts.

---

## 3. Architecture

- **AppKit only.** No SwiftUI, no WKWebView, no storyboards. The only dependency is SwiftTerm for terminal emulation.
- **One text view per pane.** Each document owns an `NSTextStorage` and an `UndoManager`. Each editor pane has one `NSLayoutManager` and `NSTextView`; switching tabs moves that layout manager onto another document's storage, so an open file costs roughly its own text. A file shown in two panes keeps one storage with a layout manager per pane, so a split costs one more text view plus the layout of what it shows.
- **TextKit 1** with non-contiguous layout, an `NSRulerView` gutter that draws only visible line numbers from a cached line index.
- **Highlighting** uses one combined `NSRegularExpression` per language and applies colors as layout-manager temporary attributes, which never modify or copy the text. Files up to 300 KB are highlighted in full, larger files around the visible range.
- **Laziness.** The terminal, the go-to-file index, folder contents, extra editor panes and the Claude Code connection are created on first use.
- **No idle work.** No polling or animations. The resource meter samples every 2 seconds only while Pulse is the active app. The Claude Code connection is a loopback socket with no timer or thread; selection changes are sent only while Claude Code is connected.

---

## 4. Memory measurements

In everyday use, with a project, several files and the terminal open, Pulse uses about 60–70 MB of physical footprint (the number Activity Monitor shows).

CI (`scripts/memory-check.sh`, GitHub macOS 14 runner) also launches the bundled app in fixed scenarios and reads physical footprint with `vmmap --summary` after 8 seconds. These fresh-launch numbers are lower than everyday use. Medians of three runs:

| Scenario | Pulse | Child processes |
|---|---|---|
| Empty window | 15.9 MB | 0 MB |
| Ten source files open | 27.1 MB | 0 MB |
| Ten files, editor split right | 29.1 MB | 0 MB |
| Ten files + terminal | 28.2 MB | 1.8 MB (shell) |
| Ten files + terminal + Claude Code connected | 28.5 MB | 1.8 MB (shell) |

The build fails if Pulse exceeds 100 MB in any scenario, and a pull request that adds more than 5 MB to any scenario needs the maintainer's approval. Numbers vary with display, font size, open files and macOS version.

---

## 5. Installation

One-line installer (downloads the latest release ZIP, installs to /Applications, clears quarantine, opens the app):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pulse0.app/install.sh | bash
```

This is the supported way to install. Releases are ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, so a Pulse.app downloaded in a browser (DMG or ZIP) is blocked by Gatekeeper ("Apple could not verify 'Pulse'…"). The installer avoids that. A copy that is already blocked can be opened from System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway, or with `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Pulse.app`.

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse
cd pulse
swift run Pulse .          # run, opening the current folder
./scripts/bundle.sh        # build dist/Pulse.app
```

Open a folder from Terminal: `pulse .`

---

## 6. Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘O | Open a folder or files |
| ⌘N | New file |
| ⇧⌘N | New window |
| ⌘S / ⇧⌘S / ⌥⌘S | Save / Save As / Save All |
| ⌘W | Close tab |
| ⌘P | Go to file |
| ⇧⌘P | Command palette |
| ⌘L | Go to line |
| ⌘F / ⌥⌘F | Find / Find and replace |
| ⌥⌘[ / ⌥⌘] | Fold / unfold |
| ⇧⌘F | Search the project |
| ⇧⌘E | Show files |
| ⌃⇧G | Show source control |
| ⌥⌘\ | Split editor right |
| ⌃` | Show or hide the terminal |
| ⌃⇧` | New terminal |
| ⌘\ | Split terminal |
| ⇧⌘K | Send selection to Claude Code |
| ⌘/ | Toggle line comment |
| ⌘] / ⌘[ | Indent / outdent |
| ⇧⌘] / ⇧⌘[ | Next / previous tab |
| ⌃⌘S | Toggle sidebar |
| ⌥⌘W | Word wrap |
| ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 | Font size |
| ⌥⌘K | Keyboard shortcuts (rebind any command) |

---

## 7. Privacy

Pulse has no telemetry or analytics and needs no account. Its only network traffic is the update check against GitHub Releases (release builds: at launch and at most once a day) and downloading an update you choose to install. The Claude Code connection is local to the Mac (127.0.0.1) and only exists while Claude Code is installed. Files never leave the Mac through Pulse.

Help › Report a Bug… and Help › Request a Feature… (the bug form also from the ladybug button at the right end of the status bar) open a GitHub issue form (https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse/issues/new/choose) in the default browser. The bug form comes with the Pulse version, macOS version and Mac model (chip and model identifier) filled in, visible and editable; nothing is posted until the user submits the issue. Pulse makes no request itself.

The website (pulse0.app) uses Google Analytics 4 only for visitors who click Accept in its cookie banner; declining loads nothing and sets no cookies.
